channel.title: Khoa Tran Engineering Portfolio - experiments
channel.description: experiments articles from Khoa Tran Engineering Portfolio.

item.title: Bloom Filters and the Capacity You Can't See Coming
item.description: Run a real bit-array Bloom filter — measure its false-positive rate against the closed-form formula, then overload it past design capacity and watch the rate climb for real, not just in a formula.

item.title: Consistent Hashing and the Rebalancing Nobody Notices
item.description: Run the real hash-ring placement algorithm against naive modulo hashing on the same key set — see how little of the keyspace a ring actually moves when a node joins or leaves, and what happens without enough virtual nodes to spread the luck around.

item.title: CRDTs: What to Do Once You Know Two Writes Are Concurrent
item.description: Run a real G-Counter against a naive LWW register, and a real OR-Set against a naive 2P-Set — see exactly which concurrent updates the naive designs silently lose, and why detecting concurrency is only half the problem.

item.title: Merkle Trees and the Diff Nobody Has to Compute
item.description: Run a real Merkle-tree targeted diff against a naive full scan on the same two datasets — see the O(1) proof of full equality, the near-O(log n) cost of a sparse diff, and the honest case where the targeted walk actually loses.

item.title: Vector Clocks and the Clock Skew That Fools Last-Write-Wins
item.description: Run the real happens-before/happens-after/concurrent test on a scripted causal history, then watch a naive last-write-wins resolver flip its answer under clock skew alone — while the causal verdict never moves.

item.title: Backpressure: Four Policies, One Overload
item.description: Block, drop-new, drop-old, and circuit breaker, run against the same producer that outruns its consumer — including proof that drop-new and drop-old discard the same number of items, but never the same ones.

item.title: Cache Freshness: What Stale-While-Revalidate Actually Buys You
item.description: Three real cache-freshness policies run against the same origin outage — TTL-blocking errors, stale-while-revalidate never blocks at all, and stale-if-error sits in between, paying for a synchronous origin attempt even when it ends up serving the same stale content SWR would have served for free.

item.title: Canary Deploys and the Sample Size Nobody Checks
item.description: A real two-proportion z-test canary analysis, run stage by stage — proving that the same real regression can go completely undetected at a small sample size and get caught at a larger one, using the exact statistic, not a story about it.

item.title: Distributed Locks: Redlock and the Pause That Breaks It
item.description: Run the real Redlock quorum algorithm against nodes you crash yourself, then simulate the exact pause Martin Kleppmann's 2016 critique is about — and see why Antirez's own rebuttal doesn't actually disagree with it.

item.title: gRPC vs REST: When the Smaller Payload Loses
item.description: A real harness measuring gRPC against REST for the same data, same server, same Go process — and REST wins throughput at every concurrency level tested for a small payload, and at half the concurrency levels tested for a 100x larger one.

item.title: Leader Election: Running the Actual Bully Algorithm, Not a Diagram of It
item.description: Crash the leader and watch the real Bully algorithm elect a new one, message by message — including the O(n^2) worst case the protocol is criticized for.

item.title: Connection Pooling: When PgBouncer Actually Helps
item.description: A real harness measuring PgBouncer against direct Postgres across two connection lifecycles — the advantage widens under one and reverses under the other, so 'add a pooler' isn't a universal answer.

item.title: Gossip Protocol Visualizer: How Cluster Membership Actually Spreads
item.description: A real push-based epidemic broadcast, run and scrubbed round by round, showing why gossip converges in O(log n) rounds instead of O(n).

item.title: Rate Limiting Algorithms: Token Bucket vs Leaky Bucket vs Fixed Window
item.description: Three rate limiting algorithms, run for real against the same burst scenario, to show what each one actually does differently — not just what it's named.

item.title: WebSockets vs Server-Sent Events: What Holding 5,000 Connections Open Actually Costs
item.description: A real harness measuring server memory for thousands of concurrent WebSocket vs SSE connections — written before the article, per the lesson from three prior benchmark rewrites.

item.title: Interactive Event Sourcing Replay
item.description: An interactive visualization of how application state is derived from an immutable, append-only event log.

item.title: Redis Streams vs BullMQ: Choosing Your Job Queue
item.description: A practical comparison of Redis Streams and BullMQ based on using both in production — covering delivery semantics, consumer group models, and failure handling patterns.

item.title: Interactive Saga State Machine Visualizer
item.description: An interactive visualization of the Saga distributed transaction pattern, demonstrating automated compensating rollbacks.

item.title: Benchmark: Event Replay in PostgreSQL vs Firestore
item.description: An interactive benchmark comparing the time it takes to replay tens of thousands of immutable events into a Read Projection.

item.title: Benchmark: Go vs TypeScript Concurrency
item.description: An interactive benchmark visualizing memory footprint and execution time for handling tens of thousands of concurrent network-bound tasks.

item.title: Queue vs Pub/Sub Comparison Notes
item.description: How delivery semantics and fan-out requirements should dictate your choice between Message Queues and Pub/Sub systems.

item.title: Throughput Simulation Notes
item.description: Experiment notes on balancing worker count and tail latency under failure pressure using client-side simulations.
